text:
alex: Heads-up — noticing a perf regression on Mixtral v1 in prod after the RoPE scaling tweak. End-to-end latency +12% for chat workloads. Profiling hints at two things: tokenizer falling back to byte-level tokens for some system prompts, and kernel fallback to byte kernels for KV updates. Dump below.

maria: Can you attach the profiler output? Is this only on Mixtral or also Qwen/Llama?

alex: Pasted small sample: 
```
profile: /tmp/prof.1769994321
hotspots:
  kv_write: 34% -> byte_kern
  attention_kern: 28% -> fallback_scalar
  tokenizer: 18% -> byte_fallback (sys_prompt)
```

li: Oh that tokenizer thing rings a bell — we recently added an extra BOS variant in chat templates which doesn't map in BPE, so it emits U+FFFD then byte fallback. More tokens -> more KV ops -> more kernel misses.

tom: Repro steps?

alex: Start convo with system prompt: "<|system|>Welcome..." on our internal chat template. On models with RoPE-scale >1.0 we see different token boundaries. Local script attached: `scripts/repro_rope_tokenizer.sh`

maria: Hypothesis: RoPE scaling changed sequence length distribution or shifted attention kernel selection thresholds leading to different kernel path. If tokenizer raises token count, batching heuristics kick in and split into smaller batches -> fewer KV reuse.

yuki: Quick mitigation: add explicit mapping for the special token to BPE mapping in tokenizer config. Also try forcing kernel selection to prefer fused kernels for Mixtral (`kernel_hint: prefer_fused`) and disable byte fallback in tokenizer as an experiment.

alex: Did both locally: mapping reduced tokens by ~6% and latency by ~7%. Forcing fused kernels gave another ~3% improvement but caused a small increase in peak memory. Logs:
```
before: tokens=512 latency=210ms mem=7.8GB
after mapping: tokens=480 latency=195ms mem=7.9GB
with fused: latency=189ms mem=8.4GB
```

li: For production, we shouldn't bump mem without commit. Can we instead warmup KV cache across shards? Maybe pre-populate with prefix cache to reduce write churn.

tom: Also check head_dim mismatch for Mixtral variants — I saw earlier that when head_dim != expected the runtime falls back to slower attention. Could be triggered by RoPE param mismatch.

maria: Action items:
- alex: push tokenizer mapping change to a canary in eu-west-1
- yuki: add kernel_hint toggle in runtime config + metric flag
- tom: add a small warmup sequence in frontend to prime KV cache for heavy chat routes
- li: watch mem and pod OOMs

perf-bot: Canary deploy started for 1769994321-tokenizer-map (canary-2) at 1769994350

alex: Canary looks good so far, tail latency down ~9% at p95. No OOMs on canary.

yuki: We'll roll kernel_hint off by default, gate it behind model= mixtral_v1 and ropescale>1.0

maria: Let's also add an eval that measures token_count_delta for our chat templates across model versions. If delta>5% trigger review.

li: I'll set alerts for token_count_delta and kv_write_rate.

alex: Thanks all. I'll link the repro script + tokenizer patch in the PR. Follow-ups tomorrow.
